children: Banking stocks bucked a sharp late selloff in the broader market on September 3, with the Nifty Bank closing 0.36 percent higher at 57,380.60 after the Reserve Bank of India's overseas capital-raising measures brought in a much stronger-than-expected $136.38 billion in foreign currency inflows under FCNR(B).

The banking index pared much of its early gains after having risen over 1 percent at intraday high, but still finished in positive territory. On the other hand, the broader market reversed sharply from a strong opening: the Sensex tumbled 417 points, or 0.55 percent, to 76,153 and the Nifty 50 fell 41 points to 23,873.

The outperformance extended across the banking space. The Nifty Private Bank index ended 0.51 percent higher, while the Nifty PSU Bank gained 0.48 percent, leaving all three banking indices among the prominent sectoral gainers at the close.
Axis Bank and HDFC Bank were among the top three gainers on the Nifty 50. Axis Bank rose 1.04 percent to Rs 1,267, while HDFC Bank gained 0.83 percent to Rs 706.65.

Within the Nifty Bank, IDFC First Bank was the biggest gainer, rising 2.83 percent to Rs 87.50, followed by IndusInd Bank, which climbed 2.74 percent to Rs 1,004.80. Yes Bank gained 1.76 percent and Union Bank of India advanced 1.15 percent. ICICI Bank and SBI finished with more modest gains of 0.25 percent and 0.24 percent, respectively.

However, the gains were not uniform. Federal Bank fell 2.48 percent, while PNB declined 0.58 percent. Kotak Mahindra Bank and AU Small Finance Bank lost 0.55 percent each, while Canara Bank and Bank of Baroda also ended lower.

Strength in financial stocks extended beyond the large-cap banking index. Bank of Maharashtra surged 5.27 percent to Rs 86.33, making it the top gainer on the BSE Midcap index. IDFC First Bank gained 2.54 percent on the BSE, while HDB Financial Services, an NBFC, advanced 2.68 percent.

The banking rally followed the RBI's disclosure that its overseas capital-raising measures had generated $136.38 billion in foreign currency inflows. FCNR(B) deposits accounted for $127.23 billion of the total as of August 31, while overseas foreign currency borrowings contributed $5.26 billion and external commercial borrowings added $3.89 billion.

The mobilisation, which substantially exceeded earlier expectations, has boosted banking-system liquidity and strengthened India's external buffers. The FCNR(B) deposit window closed on August 31, while the facilities for ECBs and OFCBs will remain open until December 31.

The inflows also supported the rupee, which strengthened sharply against the dollar during the session. The RBI had introduced the special facilities in June to attract foreign currency at a time when capital outflows, rupee weakness and elevated crude oil prices were putting pressure on India's external position.

The India VIX ended 2.24 percent lower at 11.33. Nifty Realty was the strongest sectoral performer, rising 2.58 percent, while Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 1.20 percent. Nifty IT fell 0.85 percent, Nifty FMCG lost 0.62 percent and Nifty Auto declined 0.52 percent.

title: Nifty Bank ends higher, HDFC Bank, Axis gain as RBI's FCNR(B) inflows boost lenders despite late market selloff
